proposer.mechanism: Magnitude-Conditional Chained Gate (MCCG). Maintains base AFG's primitives unchanged (single 10s rolling window of signed aggressor flow; reduce-only always submits; trade-tick subscription; look-ahead-free prune by ts_event). Two gating tiers based on adverse-flow magnitude: (a) WEAK tier: |net_flow| in [2.0, strong_threshold) -> apply base AFG's one-shot gate semantics (skip + _position_flat=True; next open unconditional, no chaining). (b) STRONG tier: |net_flow| >= strong_threshold (default 5.0) -> apply directional chain (max_chain=2): skip + record(consecutive_skips, last_skipped_side); on next same-direction order, re-evaluate gate -- if still strong-adverse, skip; if at hard cap or direction-change, force-submit + reset. The chain ONLY engages on high-magnitude readings, so it never extends skips on borderline noise. Strong-tier hard cap is 2 (not 3 like r2) to bound deferred-entry risk to ~2 oracle signals (~2s).
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: Base AFG treats |net_flow|=2 the same as |net_flow|=20: both trigger a single skip then immediate re-arm. But the conditional probability that adverse flow PERSISTS into the next 1-3s is much higher when the current reading is structurally strong (e.g. 5+ contracts in 10s) than when it is borderline (just over the 2-contract floor). Borderline cases are dominated by tick noise; strong cases reflect institutional aggressor waves that take seconds to dissipate. r2 proved chaining helps massively on persistent-adverse days; this algo applies the chain only when the magnitude warrants it, which (i) avoids over-suppression on small-magnitude false positives that drove r2's monotonic skip-rate drift, and (ii) preserves the chain edge on the heavy-loss days where r2 captured its dominant gains.
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero-cost simulator (verified from execution_algos/aggressor-flow-gate/results/backtest-results.json: mean_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0). Edge accrues entirely as realized_pnl. Base AFG: realized_pnl=$1255.5. r2 raw: $1093.25 (slightly WORSE than base AFG, only +600% vs simple). The bar for r3 is therefore to beat $1255.5 -- not just to beat simple. Falsifiable prediction: realized_pnl on the 12-day train window will exceed base AFG's $1255.5 by at least 5% (>= $1318). Failure modes: (a) if strong_threshold=5 leaves too few hits (chain rarely fires), MCCG behaves like base AFG and lands within +/- $50 of $1255.5 -- weak support; (b) if strong-tier chains over-suppress (regime resolves within 1-2s), MCCG underperforms base AFG -- falsified.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) and afg-pc-r2 (persistent-flow chain). Combines base AFG's one-shot semantics for borderline cases with r2's chain semantics for high-magnitude cases. Strictly NEVER skips less than base AFG: when |net_flow| >= 2 in adverse direction, AT LEAST one skip happens (same as base AFG); the chain only adds same-direction extension skips when the original reading was strong.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) Pure parameter sweep of r2's max_consecutive_skips (suggested in r2 NOTES): rejected -- a 1D sweep on a single param is low-information and r2 already proved 3 works; the magnitude-conditional split is structurally richer. (2) Investigate r2's monotonic skip-rate drift / state leak: deferred -- worth doing but would just produce a bug-fixed r2, not a structurally better algo. (3) Sub-window flow-acceleration confirmation (r1's burst-ratio idea, refined): rejected -- r1 proved acceleration decomposition has weak edge on this dataset (raw pnl $487.75, far below base AFG $1255.5). (4) Spread/quote-conditioned gate: rejected -- outside the aggressor-flow primitive family; would be a fundamentally new algo, not a refinement. (5) Adaptive flow_threshold via rolling sigma: rejected -- introduces a second time-varying parameter without principled scaling; r2's NOTES warned against this exact direction. (6) Higher strong_threshold (e.g. 8 or 10): defensible but starts the chain so rarely that the algorithm collapses to base AFG on most days. 5.0 (= 2.5x the base threshold) is a defensible midpoint.

objections.text: strong_threshold=5.0 is a heuristic (2.5x base threshold) with no empirical grounding. The whole mechanism hinges on the claim that |net_flow|>=5 is qualitatively different from |net_flow| in [2,5) -- but there is zero analysis of the actual distribution of net_flow magnitudes at gate-firing moments in the training data. Without this, the algo could land on the wrong inflection point and either (i) fire the chain so rarely it collapses to base AFG, or (ii) fire the chain on still-noisy readings and reproduce r2's monotonic skip-rate drift. Either run a brief EDA on one or two training dates to characterize the gate-firing |net_flow| distribution and pick a defensible threshold (e.g. the 70th or 80th percentile of gate-firing magnitudes), OR commit to a multi-threshold sweep -- not a single hand-picked value.

The chain hard cap of 2 is arbitrary and not the same as r2's 3 (which was the only empirically validated cap). The proposer offers no reason for shortening it. Two competing defensible choices: (i) keep r2's cap=3 for strict comparability, isolating the magnitude condition as the only changed variable; (ii) deliberately pick a different cap with a hypothesis-level reason (e.g., strong-tier persistence is shorter because high-magnitude bursts are themselves transient). Pick one and justify, or you cannot attribute any pnl difference to magnitude conditioning vs cap-length tuning.

Rejection of sub-window flow-confirmation (alternative #3) is too broad -- r1's specific 3s/7s burst-ratio failure does not refute simpler 'recent flow still adverse' confirmation tests. Acceptable to defer to a later run, but the rejection reasoning is weak.

Tier ordering must be explicit in the mechanism description: when |net_flow| crosses from STRONG (>=5) DOWN into WEAK ([2,5)) mid-chain, what happens? The hypothesis implicitly assumes the chain re-evaluation uses STRONG threshold; if it uses WEAK, the chain becomes harder to break than intended. Clarify which threshold is used for chain re-evaluation.

suggested_alternatives: Run a 15-minute EDA on 20260308 + 20260316 (one calm, one heavy-loss day from r2's per-date breakdown) to characterize the |net_flow| distribution at gate-firing moments, then pick strong_threshold at a defensible percentile.
Alternatively, commit to a coordinated multi-threshold sweep {3, 5, 7} with the same chain cap (r2's 3), reporting all three -- the best of three is informative.
criticizer.reasoning: The mechanism is logically coherent and meaningfully distinct from r1 and r2, but the two key parameters (strong_threshold=5, chain_cap=2) are hand-picked without empirical or hypothesis-level justification; either or both could land in the wrong regime and produce a flat or worse outcome. Pin the parameters with evidence before implementation.

proposer.mechanism: Magnitude-Conditional Chained Gate (MCCG v2). EDA-informed revision. Preserves base AFG primitives unchanged (single 10s rolling window of signed aggressor flow; reduce-only always submits; trade-tick subscription; look-ahead-free prune by ts_event). Three regimes based on |net_flow| magnitude observed at order.ts_init: (a) NEUTRAL: |net_flow| < weak_threshold (default 2.0) -> submit unconditionally (no signal). (b) WEAK ADVERSE: weak_threshold <= |net_flow| < strong_threshold AND adverse direction -> apply base AFG's one-shot gate semantics: skip + _position_flat=True; next open unconditional, no chaining. (c) STRONG ADVERSE: |net_flow| >= strong_threshold (default 50.0, the empirical p70 of fired magnitudes from EDA on 20260308 and 20260316) AND adverse direction -> apply r2-style directional chain with same hard cap (max_consecutive_skips=3, matching r2 for strict comparability): skip + record(consecutive_skips, last_skipped_side). On subsequent same-direction open orders during an active chain (consecutive_skips>=1): direction-change always force-submits and resets; hard-cap reached force-submits and resets; otherwise re-evaluate using the SAME STRONG threshold (>=50): if still strong-adverse, skip and increment; if has decayed below strong_threshold (regime weakened), force-submit and reset (do NOT fall back to weak gate during chain re-eval -- the chain only persists while the magnitude justifies it).
proposer.inefficiency_exploited: EDA on 20260308 (calm) and 20260316 (heavy-loss) reveals that base AFG's gate fires on ~96% of 1s samples (|net_flow|>=2) -- the 2.0 threshold is essentially 'any non-trivial flow', not a selectivity filter. Among fired moments, the magnitude distribution is heavy-tailed: median ~26 contracts, p70 ~50, p90 ~110-140. r2's success ($1093 vs simple $156, but ~$162 BELOW base AFG $1255) suggests chaining helps on the heavy tail (high-magnitude bursts genuinely persist) but slightly hurts on the bulk (medium-magnitude bursts are noisy and the chain extension on those is over-suppression). MCCG v2 chains ONLY on the top ~30% of magnitudes (>=50), preserving base AFG's exact one-shot behavior on the bulk middle (where AFG already extracts the dominant edge: $1255 vs $156 = +704%) while adding r2-style chain on the extreme right tail (where chaining is precision-positive).
proposer.why_survives_costs: Zero-cost simulator (verified: mean_slippage=0.0, total_commissions=0.0). Edge is realized_pnl. Bar to beat: base AFG $1255.5. Strictly NEVER skips less than base AFG (every base AFG skip happens here; chain only adds same-direction extensions on strong-tier originals). Falsifiable predictions: (i) PRIMARY: realized_pnl on the 12-day train window exceeds base AFG's $1255.5 by at least 5% (>= $1318). (ii) DIAGNOSTIC: skip rate is between base AFG's 21.6% and r2's 32.7% (because chain only engages on strong tier ~30% of AFG's skips, so additional skips beyond base AFG are bounded above by ~30% x 21.6% x avg_chain_length ~= 4-7pp on top of 21.6% -> total ~26-29%). If skip rate matches r2's 32.7% exactly, the strong-threshold is too low (chain fires too often -- behaving like r2); if skip rate is ~21.6% (= base AFG), the chain never fires (strong-threshold too high or no qualifying signals on this dataset). The 21-30% band is the meaningful-signal zone.
proposer.builds_on: aggressor-flow-gate (base) and afg-pc-r2 (persistent-flow chain). Empirically informed by EDA on training dates 20260308 and 20260316. Pins strong_threshold at the empirical p70 of fired |net_flow| values from those two dates (50 contracts), giving the chain ~30% engagement rate (vs r2's 100%). Pins max_consecutive_skips=3 for strict comparability with r2, isolating magnitude-conditioning as the only changed variable.
proposer.alternatives_considered: (1) strong_threshold lower (e.g. 5 contracts): rejected based on EDA -- ~92% of fired moments exceed 5, so chain-on-strong becomes chain-on-everything (~equivalent to r2). (2) strong_threshold even higher (e.g. p90 ~120): defensible but would suppress chain to ~10% engagement -- algo would approach base AFG too closely to show a clean differentiation. p70 is the cleanest empirical inflection from the heavy-tailed distribution. (3) Use p70 estimated daily on rolling basis (adaptive): rejected -- introduces a second time-varying parameter, more variance, less interpretable. The two EDA dates show p70 ~49 and ~52 -- highly stable -- so a constant 50 is justified. (4) Chain re-eval falls back to weak threshold: rejected -- would extend chain on decayed signals, defeating the magnitude-condition's purpose. (5) Different cap for strong vs weak tier: rejected -- weak tier doesn't chain at all, so no cap interaction. (6) Sub-window confirmation overlay: deferred -- orthogonal and could compose later.
proposer.revision_notes: Round 1 raised two MAJOR objections. (A) strong_threshold lacked empirical grounding: addressed via fresh EDA on 20260308 + 20260316 measuring 1s-sampled |net_flow| distribution. Result: at threshold=2, gate fires 95-96% of samples; fired-magnitude distribution is heavy-tailed with p70 ~50. New strong_threshold=50 is the empirical p70. (B) chain_cap=2 was unjustified: addressed by adopting r2's empirically-validated cap=3 for strict comparability, so any pnl delta is attributable to the magnitude condition rather than cap shortening. MINOR objections also addressed: tier-ordering during chain re-evaluation is now explicit (chain re-eval uses STRONG threshold; decay below strong = force-submit-and-reset). Sub-window confirmation deferred with explicit acknowledgment that r1's specific failure does not refute the family.

objections.text: The central premise -- 'chaining hurts on weak signals but helps on strong signals' -- is plausible but not directly supported by r2's breakdown. r2's per-day pnl shows the chain's $937 edge vs simple is concentrated on heavy-loss days (12, 13, 16; +619 of +937), but r2 does not instrument per-magnitude-tier chain performance, so we cannot directly confirm that the chain's marginal effect is positive on strong-tier signals and negative on weak. The supporting argument is qualitative (heavy-loss days have many strong-tier signals -> chain-on-strong captures most of r2's edge). To partially mitigate this risk, the implementation should log per-skip the |net_flow| at fire time so a post-hoc decomposition (strong-tier-chain skips vs weak-tier one-shot skips) can be done from the per-date order CSVs if the backtest disappoints.

Given the 10s rolling window and 1Hz oracle cadence, a strong-tier signal at time T is very likely (>90%) still strong at T+1 (the window shifts only 10%). The chain on strong-tier will therefore mostly hit the hard cap=3 -- effectively a fixed 'skip next 3 same-direction signals after a strong adverse reading' cooldown. This is the intended behavior but should be made explicit in the implementation notes, and the diagnostic should report mean chain length to confirm.

EDA was on 2 of 12 dates. p70 stability (49 vs 52) is reassuring but a 3rd spot-check on a mid-volume date (e.g. 20260311) would harden the choice. Not blocking; can be addressed post-hoc if the backtest result is ambiguous.

criticizer.reasoning: Round 1's two MAJOR objections were fully addressed with fresh EDA grounding the strong_threshold at the empirical p70 (~50 contracts) and aligning the chain cap with r2 for strict comparability. The residual MAJOR concern about per-tier chain performance is unavoidable without rerunning r2 with extra instrumentation, but it is bounded: the worst-case downside (chain-on-strong is also net-negative) lands the algo near base AFG with a known explanation; the upside (chain-on-strong is net-positive, capturing r2's heavy-loss-day edge without r2's weak-tier drag) clears the +5% bar. The two MINOR points are documentation/instrumentation requests, not mechanism flaws. No clearly superior untried alternative was identified within the AFG primitive family.
